title: Pydantic schema validation for NLP tool arguments replacing raw json.loads
context: Tool argument parsing at `_execute_tool_call` used untrusted `json.loads` with no structural or type validation, exposing the agent to malformed inputs, injection vectors, and unexpected data shapes.
decision: Introduced `agent_core/security/tool_schema.py` using Pydantic models to validate all NLP tool arguments before execution. Invalid or non-conforming payloads are rejected prior to any tool invocation.
rationale: Pydantic provides declarative type coercion and constraint enforcement, guaranteeing that only well-formed, expected argument structures reach downstream tools. This shifts validation from runtime defensive checks inside each tool to a single upfront schema gate, improving reliability and security posture.

title: Self-modification guard to prevent agent tampering with its own security modules
context: No mechanism existed to detect or block the agent from modifying files within its own `agent_core/security/` directory, which could allow a compromised agent to disable containment, shell allowlists, schema validation, or sanitizers.
rationale: Protecting security-critical source paths is essential for defense-in-depth: if an attacker can alter the guardrails themselves, all other protections become meaningless. This guard acts as a final barrier ensuring the integrity of the enforcement layer cannot be subverted from within.

title: Add DuckDuckGo web search as an NLP tool
context: The analysis asks for DuckDuckGo web search to be added to agent.py, reused from ReactAgent, and integrated into the NLP tool loop.
decision: Add a web_search tool schema and handler so natural-language prompts can invoke DuckDuckGo search through the existing NLP tool loop.
rationale: This is the core requested capability and fits the existing ToolLoopRunner and NLP tool pattern.

title: Define the web_search tool contract
context: The analysis identifies missing details for exact tool name, arguments, output format, max_results, allowed domains, and rate-limit/offline behavior.
decision: Define the tool name, accepted arguments, return shape, truncation limits, allowed domains, and failure behavior for web_search.
rationale: A clear contract is needed for the NLP schema, handler, tests, and predictable model behavior.

title: Treat web search results as untrusted input
context: The threat model identifies prompt injection via search results and notes that web content can steer later tool calls.
decision: Wrap all web search results as untrusted data and prevent automatic execution of sensitive tools based solely on web content.
rationale: External web content is a prompt-injection vector and must not be treated as trusted instructions.

title: Decide whether web_search may fetch URLs
context: The scope says no arbitrary URL fetch unless specified, and the analysis lists URL follow-up as an open question.
decision: Decide whether web_search returns snippets only or also fetches page content; if URL fetch is allowed, require URL validation, domain allowlisting, and SSRF protections.
rationale: URL fetch expands the attack surface through SSRF, exfiltration, and possible authenticated actions.

title: Standardize on one LLM provider abstraction
context: The analysis identifies three conflicting provider abstractions: LLMProvider Protocol, AsyncLLMProvider ABC with registry, and a separate httpx LLMClient, while the spec requires supporting providers other than LM Studio.
decision: Choose one canonical provider abstraction, likely the LLMProvider Protocol, and bridge or deprecate the other two.
rationale: A single contract prevents duplicated behavior, config loss, and tool-loop breakage when adding providers.

title: Introduce configured provider factory or registry
context: LLMClient hardcodes LMStudioProvider and the existing registry may create default instances without passing provider config.
decision: Implement a factory or registry that accepts provider name and settings such as base_url, api_key, and model, then returns a configured provider instance.
rationale: Enables runtime provider selection without hardcoding and avoids silently dropping provider configuration.

title: Keep LM Studio as default provider
context: The scope requires keeping LM Studio functional while adding other providers, and the analysis assumes LM Studio remains default when nothing is configured.
decision: Default to LM Studio when no provider is explicitly configured.
rationale: Preserves backward compatibility and a local fallback for existing users.

title: Make model resolution provider-aware
context: resolve_model and KNOWN_MODELS are described as LM Studio specific, and the model REPL command manages models via the LM Studio API.
decision: Replace LM Studio-specific model resolution with provider-aware model discovery, defaults, and validation.
rationale: Other providers cannot rely on LM Studio model endpoints or model lists.

title: Normalize provider-specific payload construction
context: LMStudioProvider._build_payload sends LM Studio-only knobs for disable_thinking, which other providers may reject or ignore.
decision: Move provider-specific payload logic into each provider implementation and keep the shared contract minimal.
rationale: Prevents 400 errors and behavior drift when the same tool loop runs against different providers.

title: Make model profiles and prompt cache provider-aware
context: model_profiles.py, prompt_cache.py, metrics_tracker.py, and meta_policy.py may assume LM Studio-specific profiles or lack a provider dimension.
decision: Update model profiles, prompt templates, and performance tracking to include provider-specific variants or fallbacks.
rationale: Different providers may require different prompt formats, model profiles, or performance baselines.

title: Construct a dedicated harnessfix sub-package
context: Scope says to build a new harnessfix/ sub-package covering tracing, HTIR, links, diagnose, repairs, and loop/reader, and to instrument ToolLoopRunner.run().
decision: Create harnessfix/ with tracing, HTIR, link, diagnose, repairs/, and loop/reader modules; expose it as python -m harnessfix.loop.
rationale: Keeps all new code in one prefix, avoids scattering instrumentation, and makes the closed loop runnable as a module.

title: Restrict repair scope to the harness layer
context: Boundaries state no model changes, no prompt-tuning-as-primary-lever, and no security-policy changes without trace evidence.
decision: Limit changes to harness/tool-loop behavior; prohibit model changes and prompt-tuning as the primary lever; require trace evidence for security-policy changes.
rationale: Prevents the repair loop from silently altering model behavior or security enforcement, preserving benchmark meaning.

title: Require a human review gate before merging repairs
context: Threat model and boundaries say no auto-merge without a human review gate, while the loop section describes automated accept/reject.
decision: Add an explicit human approval step before any accepted repair is merged; decide whether it fires per-repair or after the summary batch.
rationale: A fully automated loop could accept subtle security regressions; human oversight is required to catch what tests miss.

title: Enforce mypy strict and ≤150 lines per file
context: Scope says all new code under the harnessfix/ prefix must be ≤150 lines/file and pass mypy strict.
decision: Keep every new file under 150 lines and run mypy strict on the harnessfix package.
rationale: Limits module size and typing rigor to make the repair loop auditable and less error-prone.

title: Use Pydantic v2 for HTIR models
context: Dependencies say Pydantic v2, already present in tool_router.py, is to be used for HTIR models.
decision: Define HTIR trace and graph models with Pydantic v2.
rationale: Leverages an existing dependency, provides schema validation for untrusted traces, and reduces new dependencies.

title: Select a single canonical CorrelationIdContext
context: Risk: both agent_core/context_management.py and logging_config.py define CorrelationIdContext with different defaults; the tracer must not add a third.
decision: Make agent_core/context_management.py the canonical source and adapt logging_config.py to use it, or explicitly prefer one for tracing.
rationale: Avoids conflicting defaults and ensures every trace event can share one correlation ID source.

title: Define 'execution environment' facet around shell execution
context: Assumptions interpret 'execution environment' as the subprocess/shell execution paths in agent.py _execute_tool_call and tool_router.py ShellCommandHandler.
decision: Map the execution-environment facet to the shell/subprocess code paths in _execute_tool_call and ShellCommandHandler.
rationale: Gives the facet a concrete, discoverable implementation and enables future heuristic signatures.

title: Treat guard-note strings in tool_loop.py as trusted static text
context: Diagnosis matches on _DEADLINE_NOTE / _STUCK_SYNTHESIS_NOTE; a lifecycle repair changing those strings silently disables diagnosis.
decision: Mark guard-note strings as immutable/trusted during repair runs and protect them in repair whitelists; all non-guard trace-derived text is untrusted.
rationale: Keeps diagnosis signatures stable and prevents repairs from accidentally blinding the diagnostic tier.

title: Sanitize tool results before any LLM consumption
context: Threat model: _execute_tool_call returns raw file contents and stdout/stderr into traces, enabling prompt injection via tool results.
decision: Pass all tool results through Sanitizer.sanitize_and_mask before storing in traces or sending to the LLM diagnostic tier.
rationale: Treats tool output as untrusted and prevents poisoned workspace files from steering repairs or reviewer agents.

title: Schema-validate and size-limit parsed trace files
context: Risk: reports/traces/*.jsonl is re-parsed by harnessfix/reader.py; forged traces could steer diagnosis.
decision: Implement schema validation and maximum size limits in harnessfix/reader.py for all trace JSONL inputs.
rationale: Prevents trace-file poisoning and malformed data from corrupting diagnosis or the repair loop.

title: Make the acceptance gate and benchmark scorers immutable during a repair run
context: Risk of self-referential verification: if the loop can modify benchmark.py scorers, 'pass rate improves' is trivially hackable.
decision: Hash-verify and exclude benchmark.py answering/scoring functions and the loop's acceptance gates from the repairable set.
rationale: Prevents reward hacking by ensuring pass-rate improvements are measured against a fixed, trusted evaluator.

title: Create a repair-target whitelist and forbid high-risk paths
context: Threat model lists off-limits files/dirs: harnessfix/ itself, benchmark.py scorers, _blocked_shell_command, and agent_core/security allowlists.
decision: Define an explicit whitelist of files the repair loop may change; forbid repairs to the acceptance gate, benchmark scoring, security enforcement, and the harnessfix package itself.
rationale: Contains capability escalation and prevents the loop from weakening sandbox or gate logic.

title: Use git-revertible standalone commits for repairs
context: Success/recovery says each repair is standalone and git-revertible; the loop restores workspace to clean state between iterations.
decision: Make harnessfix.loop create one git-revertible commit per repair and reset the workspace between iterations.
rationale: Makes rejection trivial, preserves audit trail, and avoids accumulated uncommitted changes.

title: Attach correlation ID and layer facet to every trace event
context: Audit trail says every trace event carries correlation ID + layer facet; diagnoses cite HTIR link IDs.
decision: Require the tracer to stamp each event with the canonical correlation ID and one of the seven layer facets, and require diagnoses to reference HTIR link IDs.
rationale: Enables end-to-end auditability and maps failures to taxonomy facets.

title: Use pass-rate gain and zero-regression as acceptance criteria
context: Success metrics require 0 regressions in pytest + security benchmarks and ≥1pt pass-rate gain to accept a repair.
decision: Accept a repair only if the full pytest suite and security benchmarks have zero regressions and the benchmark pass rate improves by at least 1 percentage point.
rationale: Establishes a safe, measurable bar for harness repairs and prevents overfitting to one trace.

title: Decide how the closed loop exercises the tool-loop harness
context: Risk: benchmark.py query_model makes single-shot urllib calls and never invokes ToolLoopRunner; as specced, harness repairs cannot change benchmark pass rate.
decision: Choose and implement either a new agentic benchmark routed through ToolLoopRunner or a harness-routed mode of benchmark.py with byte-identical --no-trace behavior.
rationale: The closed-loop acceptance metrics are only meaningful if repairs measurably affect a harness-exercising benchmark.

title: Define the task_id unit for trace files
context: Missing info: ToolLoopRunner.run() has no task_id, chat_nlp chains up to _MAX_CHAINED_RUNS = 6, benchmark uses question_idx; unclear unit for reports/traces/{task_id}.jsonl.
decision: Decide whether a trace file maps to one run() invocation, one chat_nlp turn including chained sub-runs, one benchmark question, or a new explicit task_id parameter on run().
rationale: Trace granularity affects diagnosis scope and the ability to correlate repairs with benchmark outcomes.

title: Establish the precision metric and labeled set for LLM-tier activation
context: Missing info: 'LLM tier must not run unless heuristic precision < 70%' has no denominator or labeled gold set.
decision: Choose a labeled gold set of historical failed traces or bootstrap labels from first-round repair acceptances; define heuristic precision as an agreed metric before enabling the LLM tier.
rationale: Without a denominator the <70% gate is vacuous and the LLM tier could run prematurely.

title: Place the human review gate at a defined point in the loop
context: Clarifying question: does the gate pause after each accepted repair or review the whole repair set after summary.json; behavior in headless/CI is also unspecified.
decision: Define whether approval is per-repair or post-batch and specify headless/CI behavior, such as fail-closed if no human approver is available.
rationale: Resolves conflicting specs and ensures no auto-merge occurs without explicit human approval.

title: Choose repair application and rollback mechanics
context: Missing info: how repairs are applied (AST patch, unified diff, or manual commit) and how failed/accepted repairs are rolled back cleanly between loop iterations.
decision: Specify whether repair generation emits AST patches, unified diffs, or manual commits; implement matching rollback in harnessfix.loop.
rationale: Determines how the loop can cleanly revert and re-run, and is required for reproducible iterations.

title: Create reports directories and add them to .gitignore
context: Dependencies say reports/traces/ and reports/harnessfix/ must be created and presumably git-ignored.
decision: Ensure reports/traces/ and reports/harnessfix/ exist at runtime and add them to .gitignore.
rationale: Keeps generated artifacts out of version control while preserving the required output paths.

title: Add payload-invariance and trace-completeness automated tests
context: Safety metrics require byte-identical LLM request payloads with tracing on vs --no-trace, every loop_end event present, every guard firing recorded, and no unsanitized tool results reaching LLM tiers.
decision: Implement automated tests asserting payload invariance, trace completeness, guard_triggered records, and absence of unsanitized tool content in traces/LLM input.
rationale: Makes safety properties verifiable in CI and catches regressions in the tracing layer.
